query: What additive manufacturing strategy and post-processing route can enable the fabrication of a refractory high-entropy alloy family (Group IV-V transition metals) capable of retaining high-temperature structural integrity, and what specific microstructural state is hypothesized to optimize mechanical performance while mitigating the inherent brittleness associated with interstitial impurities?

generation.hypothesis: Fabrication of a Group IV-V refractory high-entropy alloy (e.g., WTaMoNbV) via Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) using mixed elemental powders, followed by a high-temperature Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) treatment at 1100–1200 °C, will yield a chemically homogeneous single-phase BCC microstructure with sub-micron grain size and negligible porosity, thereby mitigating the brittleness caused by interstitial impurities and elemental segregation while retaining high-temperature structural integrity.
generation.material_initial_state: Mixed elemental powders of Group IV-V transition metals (e.g., W, Ta, Mo, Nb, V) with irregular morphology and varying melting points, containing potential interstitial impurities (O, N, C) and prone to segregation during solidification.
generation.intervention: Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) using a high-energy density laser to melt mixed elemental powders, followed by post-processing via High Isostatic Pressing (HIP) at 1100–1200 °C for 2 hours in an inert atmosphere.
generation.conditions: Processing in a pure argon atmosphere (to minimize interstitial uptake), with layer thickness ~30–100 μm and volumetric energy density optimized to achieve >95% density; HIP performed at temperatures sufficient to dissolve precipitates but below the melting point of the primary BCC phase.
generation.structural_mediator: Rapid solidification-induced refinement of the BCC matrix combined with HIP-driven elimination of lack-of-fusion defects, dissolution of V-rich intergranular precipitates, and homogenization of elemental segregation.
generation.mechanism: The rapid cooling rates in LPBF suppress the formation of brittle intermetallic compounds and refine the grain structure, while the subsequent HIP treatment relieves residual stresses, closes internal pores, and dissolves segregation-induced precipitates (e.g., V-rich phases) that act as crack initiation sites, effectively mitigating the brittleness associated with impurities and segregation.
generation.predicted_outcome: The HIP-treated LPBF alloy will exhibit a uniform single-phase BCC microstructure with a grain size <10 μm, near-theoretical density (>99%), and significantly improved ductility and fracture toughness compared to as-built LPBF samples and arc-melted counterparts, while maintaining high compressive strength at elevated temperatures.
generation.baseline: As-built LPBF samples of WTaMoNbV which exhibit high porosity (up to 62% in early trials), elemental segregation (V at grain boundaries), and brittle fracture behavior due to lack-of-fusion defects and residual stresses.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies specifically to refractory HEAs with Group IV-V elements processed via LPBF where the melting point disparity between elements (e.g., V vs. W) drives segregation; it assumes the HIP temperature does not induce grain coarsening or phase decomposition into brittle intermetallics.
generation.uncertainty: While HIP is known to remove defects in other HEAs (PMC7512523), the specific interaction between HIP parameters and the high melting point disparity in WTaMoNbV (PMC9229239) is not fully characterized; there is uncertainty regarding whether the specific interstitial impurity levels in mixed elemental powders can be fully mitigated without prior powder pre-treatment, and whether the high-temperature HIP might induce unwanted phase transformations in this specific refractory system.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate WTaMoNbV alloys via LPBF using mixed elemental powders. Divide samples into two groups: (1) As-built, and (2) Post-HIP treated at 1150 °C for 2 h. Perform microstructural analysis (SEM/TEM) to quantify porosity, grain size, and elemental segregation, followed by compression testing at room temperature and 800 °C to measure ductility and strength.
measurements: Compressive yield strength and fracture strain at RT and 800 °C
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the HIP-treated samples show no significant reduction in porosity (<5% improvement), no dissolution of V-rich intergranular precipitates, or if the ductility (fracture strain) does not increase by at least 20% compared to the as-built samples, or if the HIP treatment induces the formation of brittle secondary phases.

Question: Can refractory high-entropy alloy WTaMoNbV be adequately synthesized via a laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) process using mixed elemental alloying powder as the raw material, and how do its properties compare to a counterpart produced by arc melting furnace (AMF)?. System: Refractory High-Entropy Alloy WTaMoNbV (20 at% W, 20 at% Ta, 20 at% Mo, 20 at% Nb, 20 at% V).
